newsitem.title: USA: Interval Research to form three startup companies.
newsitem.headline: Interval Research to form three startup companies.

text.p: Interval Research Corp, founded four years ago by Microsoft Corp co-founder Paul Allen, said on Wednesday it would form three startup companies to pursue commercial endeavors.

The three companies -- Carnelian Inc, Ogopogo Studios and Purple Moon -- stemmed from several of the privately held company's high-technology research initiatives. They represented Interval's first commercial activity, it said.
Carnelian would aim to become a leading supplier of software systems for Internet publishing, it said.
Ogopogo Studios designs and produces novel, technology based entertainment which enabled children ages six to 11 years old to have unprecedented control of their play environment, Interval said.
The company's products are based on research that combined interaction design, signal processing technology and studies on the nature of children's play, Interval said.
Purple Moon will develop, publish and market interactive media designed especially for girls, Interval said.
The three companies would pursue commerical ventures after conducting long-term research at Interval, Interval said.

"We're pleased that after four years, we already have explored and tested some ideas and technologies that show commercial promise," said David Liddle, Interval Research chief executive officer, who founded the company with Allen. "We hope for more start-ups over the coming years."

Each of the new companies has been launched with staff, intellectual property and initial funding provided by Interval. But to gain critical management attention inherent in venture capital funding, the companies would likely seek such funding during the next several months, Interval said.
